one_month_reasoning: The main event in the window is Q3 2026 earnings. The date is not confirmed in what I found, but the pattern (Q3 2025 on Oct 30, Q2 2026 on July 30) puts it around Oct 29-30, before the Oct 30 close (Oct 31 is a Saturday). Quanta beat by about 30% in both Q1 and Q2 2026 and the stock jumped ~16% on the Q2 print, but much of that is now in consensus ($16.74 for 2026 against the $16.45-16.95 guide), and the stock gave back the post-Q2 gains within a month. Hyperscaler Q3 capex guides (late October) and the Texas data-center permitting pause (audit due mid-December) are the other inputs. I see no clear direction: a small upside skew from the beat history roughly cancels the risk of a 'beat but de-rate' reaction. So I use a nearly symmetric lognormal centered at $664, with sigma 14% (the 12.6% baseline monthly vol plus an earnings premium).

fair_value.method: Blend of 30x Oct-2027 NTM adj EPS of $21.1 ($633, 50%), 19x NTM EBITDA of $5.3B less $5.5B net debt ($624, 30%) and a 3% FCF yield on 2027E FCF of $2.7B ($590, 20%), giving ~$620. That is slightly below the $662.6 spot because I assume further multiple compression while earnings grow ~15-17%.

bear.story: AI and data-center capex digestion (2027 hyperscaler capex growth slows from ~80% to ~20% or lower), spreading state permitting pauses (Texas, New York), and possibly a recession (Polymarket 35% / Kalshi 24%). NTM EPS slips to ~$18 and the multiple falls to ~22x, closer to contractor peers. Debt-funded M&A and a $2.9B+ build in contract assets and unbilled receivables add risk.

base.story: Guidance is met and 2027 adj EPS comes in around $19-19.6. The multiple drifts from ~35x to ~30x NTM as growth normalizes toward the 15-20% long-term plan, so the stock goes roughly sideways, with earnings growth offsetting de-rating.

bull.story: Another round of 25%+ beats; transmission and generation megaprojects ramp in 2H27; labor-scarcity pricing power (the Bernstein thesis). NTM EPS reaches ~$24 and the multiple holds at ~38x.

thesis_break_reason: At $480 the stock would trade at ~24x 2027 consensus adj EPS, a level the market would likely only accept if expected earnings were falling: a 2027 guide below consensus, backlog decline, cancellation of data-center or large transmission work, or a sector-wide AI-capex retrenchment. It is ~28% below spot, which is more than one standard deviation of ordinary drift at 44% vol over ~8 months, and close to the low end of sell-side targets ($410).

reasoning: Starting point: $662.6, 44% realized vol. The fundamentals are strong. Q2 2026 beat by ~29% on EPS, backlog is a record $53.4B, and 2026 adj EPS guidance is $16.45-16.95 (+55% YoY), so a short or fraud case does not hold up. I found no short-seller report, no material weakness, no 10%+ customer, and credit is investment grade (Baa3, outlook positive; new notes at 4.85-5.55%) with debt/EBITDA of 1.7x. The bear case is about valuation and the cycle, not solvency. (1) Valuation: ~40x 2026 adj EPS and ~57x GAAP, EV/EBITDA ~26x. JPM (Neutral, $714), BMO and Benchmark (Sell) downgraded explicitly on valuation, and the forward P/E has already de-rated from ~50x to ~35x. (2) Demand risk: Texas paused data-center interconnections (Aug 3) and then all permits (Sept 21) until an audit due mid-December; New York and 116+ municipalities have moratoria; technology is 15-20% of Quanta revenue; consensus 2027 hyperscaler capex growth slows to ~20-25%. (3) Quality: adj EPS runs ~43% above GAAP because of acquisition amortization and stock comp, M&A is serial and debt-funded ($2B of notes in August), receivables are growing fast, and the CEO sold $120M near the highs in May. Weighing these honestly: earnings should still grow ~15-17%, so the realistic downside is a de-rating to ~30x rather than a collapse. My fair value is ~$620 (P/E, EV/EBITDA and FCF blend) and the scenario mean is ~$660 (25% at $400, 50% at $645, 25% at $920). For the ladder I used a mixture: 85% lognormal (median $665, sigma 0.36) plus a 15% crash component (median $470, sigma 0.35) for the AI-capex or recession left tail. The result has a median of ~$640, P(>=spot) of 0.45, and a fatter left tail than a plain lognormal. Limitations: Twelve Data fundamentals and insider endpoints need a paid plan; a curl fetch of some SEC 8-K exhibits was blocked, so I relied on press-release and 10-Q pages through WebFetch; prediction-market volumes were not reachable (403/429), so the recession odds are qualitative inputs only and come from search snippets. The 2027 consensus EPS comes from a search snippet of Yahoo Finance because the page did not render.
